reason: The image-only reading left the short line fragments unconnected and several words unresolved ('ozoe', 'isis', 'lari', 'festinatu..te', 't̄n bn̄ ꝑci', 'fra'); reread with lat. 15951 in hand they resolved as orationes, [in]simul, [sigil]latim, festiva(ve)runt, bien procu[rat] and fid[eles], and the three passages fell into the sermon's order.
sources: Paris, BnF, lat. 15951, ff. 336rb-336va, sermon Congregate illi sanctos eius, with the marginal note 'fr. N. de biart.' on f. 336r; Gallica btv1b90672729, views 360-361, page images

J. B. Schneyer, Repertorium der lateinischen Sermones des Mittelalters, vol. 4, p. 244 (Nicolaus de Byard, Sermones de sanctis no. 194) and vol. 5, no. 2016 (Robert of Sorbon); listing not rechecked on the page
text:
Source-assisted selected reading of F-ln58 (Antwerpen, Erfgoedbibliotheek Hendrik Conscience, Fragm. 297 a-b), piece A only. Lines reread on the native images: recto column b, lines 10-15; verso column a, lines 1-14; verso column b, lines 1-11. A research reader who knew the sermon's opening words from Schneyer read these lines before opening Paris, BnF, lat. 15951, and reread a few afterwards (recto b, line 14); an independent checker reread recto b, lines 12-15, verso a, lines 9-14, and verso b, lines 1-11, on the native images before opening lat. 15951 at those places, and its readings are given where they differ. Recto column a, recto column b, lines 1-9, and both faces of piece B rest on the image-only first reading (a few words checked by the research reader) and are not matched. Line numbers count from the top of each column on the face. (..) = expansion; [..] = lost at the cut or supplied; (?) = uncertain; ^x^ = written above the line; ⁊ = et; ꝯ = con; ꝓ = pro; ꝑ = per. Regions are x,y,width,height in native pixels.
